articles.title: The Winamp Skin Museum lets you relive the wonderful chaos of late-’90s computing
articles.summary: Remember Winamp? Remember Winamp skins? If you grew up using a computer in the late ‘90s or early ‘00s, then you probably do. If so, the Winamp Skin Museum is for you — a nostalgic collection of some 65,000 skins, all fully interactive and usable.
articles.body: Every now and again, individuals of a certain generation (my generation) have a tendency to fall into a catatonic state whenever we remember Winamp skins. There’s just something about them that instantly transports one back to the late ‘90s / early ‘00s, when user interfaces were truly customizable, and your music collection was an endless and engrossing battle against garbled filenames like LINKIN_PORK-IN%THE%END(HQ).mp3. If any of that is triggering a nostalgic response, then you’ll probably enjoy the Winamp Skin Museum. It’s an endlessly scrolling collection of 65,000 Winamp skins, searchable and fully interactive. There’s a default playlist (which includes the “Llama Whippin’ Intro”), and you can even load audio files into it from your computer, if you happen to have any lying around. [Media: The skins were previously collected on the Internet Archive but assembled into this new accessible format by Facebook engineer Jordan Eldredge. On Twitter, Eldredge notes he’s still taking collections for the project if you have any skins you want to donate, and he describes the collection as capturing “an iconic moment in internet art history.” He’s not wrong. The taste on display in the Winamp Skin Museum is, in a word, stunning. It has all of the artistic value of a national art gallery, but it focuses in on late-’90s / early-’00s aesthetics with enough raw energy to bring back nü metal. On display, you can see anime skins, gaming skins, communist skins, sci-fi skins, skins dedicated to particular artists, and a cornucopia of indescribable vibes in between. The only disappointment is that the format of the museum doesn’t lend itself to supporting the stranger skins that transformed the size and shape of Winamp’s various elements. But perhaps that would have been too much for today’s modern, sleek UIs to handle. [Image: You can even load up visualizations. This is the weird thing about Winamp skins, though: they don’t just capture a visual aesthetic, but a mode of interaction with technology. Personally, they remind me of an era when it felt like I had more control over my computer. I could customize Winamp skins, sure, but also my whole desktop, down to my extremely carefully collated music collection. There was also something about having to sort through files and dig up album art that encouraged a sort of engagement with music that feels, to me, very different to today’s streaming model. Spotify, compared to Winamp, seems passive. You’ll get your Discover playlist, and you’ll like it. (And I do.) You could argue that we’ve traded into this chaotic customization for convenience. But was it worth it? Probably. Perhaps all I’m really missing is a period of my life when I had time and energy to mess about with that sort of thing. Arguably, computers are just as customizable, if you care to put in the effort. But you see what I mean, now? Winamp skins, dude. They really take you back.

articles.title: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man gets community justice right
articles.summary: The most interesting thing about Disney Plus’ Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is its focus on making Peter Parker a hero of the people.
articles.body: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man star Hudson Thames left many eyebrows raised last week after his comments about fearing the Disney Plus series would be “annoying and woke.” During a subsequent Reddit AMA, series creator Jeff Trammell was quick to start doing damage control, and he insisted that Thames had misspoken. But even in its most charitable interpretation, Thames’ statement was pretty odd considering how being annoying and constantly vigilant about injustice are kind of Spider-Man’s whole schtick. We may never know exactly what Thames meant or whether his feelings could have been expressed more thoughtfully. But what’s funny about the entire situation is how Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is, in fact, one of those “woke” shows you’re always hearing culturally conservative types harp on about. It celebrates multiculturalism by treating diversity as a simple fact of the world Peter Parker exists in. And the series’s “wokeness” is honestly one of the best things about it. There’s a lot of the Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man series that rings familiar if you’ve spent time reading Marvel’s comics or watched any of the studio’s multiple TV shows or films revolving around the webhead. It’s another story about Peter Parker (Thames), a dorky kid from Queens trying to balance a double life as both a high school student and a superhero. Some of the series’s worldbuilding details are a little different than what you might be used to; Aunt May (Kari Wahlgren) loses her husband before Peter is bitten by a strange spider, for example. But the show hits many of the classic Spider-Man beats, like Peter’s trademark bad luck and his aptitude for building gadgets like his webshooters. [Media: The show’s biggest changes come by way of the friends and rivals Peter makes as he bounces back and forth between classes at school and an internship at Norman Osborn’s (Colman Domingo) Oscorp. More traditional Spider-Man characters like Harry Osborn (Zeno Robinson) and Lonnie Lincoln (Eugene Byrd) are also in the mix. But this Peter is best buds with longtime Runaways fixture Nico Minoru (Grace Song), and both have crushes on Pearl Pangan (Cathy Ang) — a newer character who first appeared in Marvel’s War of the Realms comics event back in 2019. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is not the first instance of Marvel diversifying the cast of supporting characters around Peter Parker in order to make Spider-Man stories more inclusive and reflective of what life can be like in New York City. Those changes were part of what made 2008’s The Spectacular Spider-Man animated series and Marvel / Sony’s recent live-action Spider-Man films feel so modern compared to Stan Lee and Steve Ditko’s early Spider-Man comics from the ’60s in which the vast majority of characters were white. Your Friendly Neighborhood’s diversity isn’t the only thing it has going for it. The show’s action, though stutter-y at times, is fun and works well with its cel-shaded, comic book-inspired aesthetic that often presents shots as if they were panels from a physical book. But the series’s slight adjustments to Peter Parker’s world are what gives its story a level of depth and thoughtfulness — which could be considered “woke” — that is surprising to see from Marvel. It bears repeating that, even though the term “woke” has become a racist / sexist / homophobic catchall dogwhistle often used by bigots as a pejorative, the concept of staying woke originated within Black communities and refers to the importance of being able to recognize the societal dangers Black people face. Featuring characters who are Black, or merely non-white, does not automatically mean that a film or TV show has anything to say about things like policing, crime, and structural inequality. But Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man certainly does as it starts showing you what makes this Peter Parker more of a street-level vigilante than any of his big-screen counterparts. [Image: Even though certain characters’ names give you an idea of the more fantastical nonsense Peter’s going to end up dealing with as the season continues, one of the first bits of heroism we see from him in the premiere is a quick moment where he brings a thief back to a pizza joint she’s just robbed. The thief, a white woman, tells Peter that she’s become desperate after losing her job. Peter has no way to know if that story is true, but as part of a family dealing with their own money problems, he can understand how that kind of loss pushes people to the edge. That moment contrasts sharply with another scene where Lonnie, who is Black, is racially profiled in quick succession by both the police on the street and a random white woman on the train as he makes his way home. Through that juxtaposition of moments, Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is actually saying a lot about how different styles of policing communities can lead to drastically different outcomes for their populations. The show does not need to depict the police attacking Lonnie to illustrate how racial profiling is a kind of violence in and of itself that causes real harm to the people who experience it. We also don’t need to know every detail of the pizza thief’s life to grasp the difficulty of her circumstances and see how Spider-Man was able to peacefully resolve a criminal situation by leading with empathy rather than suspicion. Before the concept of wokeness was co-opted and weaponized by the right, it was very easy to understand as being aware of and attentive to social inequalities that shape our world. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man might not explicitly spell them out, but those ideas are baked into its take on Peter Parker. A lot of this — the focus on community, the desire to help rather than penalize — has always been part of the traditional Spider-Man brand. And Disney’s new show is doing an excellent job of making sure you don’t forget that.

articles.title: Netflix’s series about the FTX fiasco has found its leading effective altruists
articles.summary: Netflix’s The Altruists has cast Anthony Boyle as Sam Bankman-Fried and Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison.
articles.body: Like Amazon and Apple, Netflix is also looking to cash in on the story of how Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison managed to steal billions from the FTX cryptocurrency exchange. Variety reports that Anthony Boyle (Tetris, Manhunt) and Julia Garner (Ozark, The Fantastic Four: First Steps) have been cast in Netflix’s upcoming drama series The Altruists as Bankman-Fried and Ellison. Executive produced by Graham Moore and Jacqueline Hoyt (who will also showrun the series), The Altruists will recount how Bankman-Fried, FTX’s former CEO, and Ellison, the former head of FTX’s sister cryptocurrency trading firm, Alameda Research, enriched themselves by defrauding FTX’s investors. Netflix has ordered eight episodes for the series, and James Ponsoldt (Shrinking, Running Point) is attached to direct the premiere. Netflix describes the series as being about “two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye — and then seduced, coaxed, and teased each other into stealing $8 billion,” which sounds accurate, if a bit aggrandizing. Presumably, the show will cover how both Bankman-Fried and Ellison ultimately wound up being sentenced to 25 and two years in prison, respectively. And if The Altruists really wants to be seen as a serious, thoughtful piece of storytelling that isn’t just mythologizing its central felons, it should probably touch on how hard Bankman-Fried is now pushing for Donald Trump to give him a pardon. (Disclosure: The Altruists is a coproduction by Higher Ground Productions and New York Magazine/Vox Media Studios.) Correction, May 29th: An earlier version of this article incorrectly stated that Bankman-Fried pleaded guilty to the charges against him. He pleaded not guilty before he was subsequently sentenced to 25 years.

articles.title: Aluno em SP agride funcionários e quebra academia na Oscar Freire | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo professor, homem foi ao local para cobrar um adiantamento que fez ao personal trainer; ele teria arremessado notebook contra gerente e retornado nesta manhã para depredar o estabelecimento.
articles.summary: Segundo professor, homem foi ao local para cobrar um adiantamento que fez ao personal trainer; ele teria arremessado notebook contra gerente e retornado nesta manhã para depredar o estabelecimento.
articles.body:
Um aluno de uma academia localizada na Rua Oscar Freire, 1411, em Pinheiros, área nobre de São Paulo , agrediu funcionários na última quarta-feira (7) e, nesta quinta-feira (8), retornou ao local e quebrou espelhos da unidade. Câmeras de segurança registraram o ataque (veja acima).

Pelas imagens, de ângulos diferentes, é possível ver que ele parte para cima do gerente, e depois é apartado por um professor. Ele também pega os pesos da academia e joga contra os espelhos. Alguns alunos saem correndo. Há ainda imagens dele arremeçando um notebook contra uma funcionária.

Segundo o gerente da academia, Rubens Abrego Lourenço da Silva, de 47 anos, o homem foi ao local inicialmente para cobrar um valor de R$ 1.300 que teria emprestado a um personal trainer que atende na unidade. O nome do agressor ainda não foi divulgado.

"O problema com esse aluno começou na segunda-feira. Ele contrata um personal e é aluno da academia, pagante da academia, e como aluno ele contrata um personal por fora, para ter a aula assistida. Aí ele diz que o personal solicitou R$ 1.300 emprestado para ele", afirmou o gerente em entrevista ao g1.

Aluno invade academia na Oscar Freire e quebra espelhos — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com o relato, o personal teria pedido o adiantamento do valor, mas está afastado por problemas de saúde e não está indo ao local dar as aulas. O aluno, então, teria procurado a academia para cobrar o dinheiro.

O gerente disse que consultou a diretoria e recebeu a orientação de que a academia não poderia se responsabilizar pelo valor, já que o acordo teria sido feito diretamente entre o aluno e o personal trainer.

Segundo o gerente, o aluno não aceitou a explicação por telefone e foi até a academia cerca de 15 minutos depois da ligação. No local, ele teria ameaçado e agredido verbalmente funcionários.

"Deu 15 minutos ele foi na academia, começou a fazer um espetáculo lá na frente da recepção, chamar a gente de 'bandido', me chamou de 'ladrão', falou que a gente não paga para funcionar, começou a falar um monte de absurdo", declarou.

Ainda segundo o gerente, o homem passou a bater no balcão da recepção. A gerente começou a filmar a situação e, conforme o relato, ele teria tentado agredi-la algumas vezes.

"Ele viu que a gente não estava dando bola, começou a bater no balcão, a nossa gerente começou a filmar, ele ficou nervoso, tentou agredí-la duas, três vezes, na quarta vez ele pega o notebook que está na mesa, dá um tapa no notebook, acerta o peito dela", disse.

Gerente da academia onde aluno quebrou vidros e agrediu funcionários — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O gerente afirmou que acionou a polícia durante a confusão. Ainda de acordo com o relato, o aluno teria entrado na área da recepção e dito que pegaria o dinheiro que estava na gaveta.

"Depois ele tenta invadir, falou que ia roubar o dinheiro de volta, que ia pegar o dinheiro da gaveta, e aí eu abordo ele lá, a gente começa uma luta corporal praticamente", contou.

O gerente disse que registrou um boletim de ocorrência sobre o episódio ocorrido na quarta-feira (7), mas que o homem não foi preso em flagrante.

Nesta quinta-feira (8), segundo o gerente, o aluno voltou à academia por volta das 7h e teria ameaçado os funcionários. Ele teria exigido que as imagens da confusão fossem apagadas.

"Hoje, ele voltou, ameaçando, 7h da manhã ele voltou, mandando apagar todas as imagens, que se continuar essas imagens ele ia acabar com todo mundo, ameaçando a gerente e a mim", afirmou.

Ainda segundo o gerente, cerca de 40 minutos depois, o homem retornou ao estabelecimento e começou a quebrar os espelhos da academia. Imagens mostram o momento em que alunos deixam o local durante o ataque.

O gerente e a gerente estão no 14º Distrito Policial, onde, segundo o relato, devem registrar boletim de ocorrência por agressão e danos ao patrimônio.

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s mortal remains brought to Pune for state funeral, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis pays last respects, Eknath Shinde, 'Welcome' director Anees Bazmee and others arrive
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, was accorded a state funeral
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away on Thursday at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa, was accorded a state funeral in recognition of his contribution to theatre and cinema. His mortal remains have now been brought to Donje in Pune, where his last rites will be performed, and several celebrities and prominent personalities have begun arriving to pay their final respects.Nana Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his Goa residence and was given continuous CPR for around 45 minutes. He died at 5:20 am. His son, Malhar, confirmed the news to The Indian Express and said, “Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons."Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced that Nana would be accorded a state funeral, recognising his immense contribution to theatre and cinema. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also paid his last respects to the actor at Pune Airport after his mortal remains arrived from Goa.The mortal remains were subsequently taken from the airport to Donje village, where the final rites are being held. As Nana’s mortal remains have reached the farmhouse, members of the film industry and political fraternity have started arriving to pay their last respects to the veteran actor.Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was among the first prominent personalities to reach the venue for Nana Patekar’s funeral. More celebrities and well-wishers are expected to arrive in Donje as the actor’s final journey continues. Filmmaker Anees Bazmi, actor-director Pravin Tarde, Prasad Oak among others were also spotted at the funeral.Nana Patekar's last films will be 'Shakti Shalini' starring Aneet Padda and 'Eetha' starring Shraddha Kapoor.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Exclusive: Dimple Kapadia on Nana Patekar: He was generous & brutally honest, perhaps why he was often misunderstood
articles.summary: Dimple Kapadia and Nana Patekar worked together in four films, including Krantiveer (1994) and Prahaar: The Final Attack (1991), both of which became
articles.body: Dimple Kapadia and Nana Patekar worked together in four films, including Krantiveer (1994) and Prahaar: The Final Attack (1991), both of which became iconic for capturing the angst, frustration and helplessness of common man and the middle class. Prahaar was the only feature film Nana directed in his career, with Dimple, Madhuri Dixit and Gautam Joglekar among its cast.Shaken by the news of Nana’s untimely demise, Dimple says she is still struggling to process the loss. “It’s unbelievable. It’s not sinking in. I wanted to call him the other day, but I delayed it and now I can’t speak to him ever. I wish I had made that call. I won’t be able to get over this.”Looking back at their journey and friendship, she recalls Nana as an actor and co-star who was deeply invested in his colleagues. “He was a fine actor and a great co-star who was always giving. It was wonderful to work with him because he wasn’t selfish. He cared about how I would look in a scene too, and how my character came across. That’s rare.”On a personal note, she says, “Nana was brutally honest. He never minced his words. If he wanted to say something to you, he would say it to your face. That was perhaps why he was often misunderstood. But he always said things for your own good. The intent was your bhalai. He wasn’t rude, just unfiltered and well-intentioned. There was an angst all over his face, but he was extremely warm and caring as a person.”Dimple remembers several instances of his spontaneous interventions on set. “There was a courtroom scene in one of our films where I had to be teary-eyed, and he would yell at me from a distance, ‘Aiyee Dimpy, glycerine nahi use karneka.’” She laughs, recalling how Nana never hesitated to push his co-stars to give their best.She also remembers a scene in another film where Nana’s character was supposed to investigate hers. “I am shown putting my knitting needles aside when he enters. He saw the prop and started knitting himself. For a man to do that was powerful and spontaneous. It made the scene look organic and impactful.”Dimple is particularly grateful that she got to experience Nana not just as an actor but as a director. “I’m glad I was directed by Nana in Prahaar. Was he calm on set as a director? Not at all. He was totally mad,” she says with a smile. “But there was so much to learn from him as an artiste and as a person.”Reflecting on their much-loved pairing in Krantiveer, she adds, “We fed off each other’s energy in Krantiveer. This is such a great loss for Hindi cinema, Marathi cinema and theatre. I’m going to miss him and his simplicity.”Author: Renuka.Vyavahare@timesofindia.com Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Nana Patekar laid to rest with full state honours in Pune, Eknath Shinde offers floral tribute, Jackie Shroff and thousands of fans gather to bid tearful farewell to the legendary actor
articles.summary: Legendary actor Nana Patekar breathed his last on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa at the age of 75.
articles.body: Legendary actor Nana Patekar breathed his last on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa at the age of 75. The veteran actor suffered a cardiac arrest and doctors attempted to revive him with continuous CPR for around 45 minutes. He was declared dead at around 5:20 am.Nana’s son Malhar confirmed the news to The Indian Express and said, “Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons.”In recognition of his immense contribution to theatre and cinema, the Maharashtra government accorded Nana Patekar a state funeral. His mortal remains were brought to Pune, where his last rites were performed at his farmhouse in Donje with full state honours. Large numbers of fans gathered to pay their final respects to the actor, whose powerful performances over a career spanning several decades made him one of Indian cinema’s most respected performers.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis paid his last respects to Nana at Pune Airport after his mortal remains arrived from Goa. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was also among the prominent personalities who reached the venue to bid farewell to the veteran actor.Nana’s death has also left the film fraternity mourning. Several Bollywood celebrities took to social media to remember the actor and share personal memories of him.Shah Rukh Khan, who worked with Nana in ‘Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman’ and ‘Shakti: The Power’, shared an emotional note recalling the veteran actor as his mentor, teacher, critic and friend. Remembering their first meeting, SRK wrote, “When I first met him, out of awe and awkwardness I fiddled with my hair. He slapped my hand away and said ‘hero ki tarah Baal mat bana...tu actor hai’!”He further remembered Nana’s candid nature and wrote, “He didn’t flatter you. He didn’t tell you what you wanted to hear. He told you what you needed to hear. That was Nana. Straightforward. Rough, honest and had the most beautiful smile.” SRK also recalled their carrom games and ended his tribute by calling Nana a “masterful actor and an unbeatable carrom champion.”Salman Khan also paid tribute to Nana on Instagram, sharing a picture of the late actor and writing, “Nanaaaaaaaaaaa. Rest in peace bhau…”Ajay Devgn, who shared screen space with Nana in films including ‘Apaharan’ and ‘Raajneeti’, posted an old picture with the actor and wrote, “Not many made us happy, sad and feel anger quite the way Nana did. His presence was powerful, his performances unforgettable, and his absence will now be deeply felt. Rest well, Nana…Om Shanti.”Several other members of the film fraternity, including Akshay Kumar, Paresh Rawal, Manisha Koirala, Manoj Bajpayee, Urmila Matondkar, Alia Bhatt, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Karan Johar, also remembered Nana Patekar on social media, mourning the loss of one of Indian cinema’s most distinctive and powerful actors.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sean Combs' release date is delayed following prison perks allegations
articles.summary: Sean Combs' release date from FCI Fort Dix was pushed back following allegations of a pampered prison lifestyle. His new release date is set for March 2, 202...
articles.body:
Sean "Diddy" Combs' release date has been pushed back following allegations of a plush prison lifestyle.

The disgraced music mogul is currently serving a 50-month sentence after he was convicted of transporting prostitutes across state lines for drug-fueled sex performances known as "freak-offs."

While earlier October reports indicated that the artist and producer would be released on Jan. 21, 2028 — which shaved months off his original June 2028 discharge — an updated search on the Federal Bureau of Prisons inmate database reveals his new revised date as March 2, 2028.

News of his release date comes as the "Bad Boy for Life" singer was reportedly placed and remained in solitary confinement at FCI Fort Dix, a low-security federal prison in New Jersey, following allegations of a pampered prison lifestyle.

On Sept. 29, an NBC report detailed the accounts of four anonymous inmates who claim that the 56-year-old had been paying men for special services.

Sources told NBC News that Combs paid inmates to clean and cook special meals for him, including curry chicken, pizza and empanadas, and that the hip-hop and R&B music producer also receives Chinese-style massages.

To pay for the labor, inmates allege that individuals outside of the prison are depositing thousands of dollars into the commissary accounts of those waiting on the "Satisfy You" singer.

The news outlet also published an image of Combs using a contraband phone, a prohibited item across state and federal prisons; multiple inmates said that he uses it to scroll Instagram and view explicit nude content shared by an old girlfriend.

Two sources also shared that Diddy has access to a "jailbroken" tablet where he watches movies and documentaries, including "Sean Combs: The Reckoning," the Netflix docuseries produced by his adversary Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson.

Sources also allege that Combs is smuggling an illegal stash of alcohol and purchasing an antidepressant drug known as Remeron, or "rem-roms," from other inmates.

"This is not some normal s— you see in jail. This is some rich s—. It looks crazy, but again, it's Diddy," one source told NBC.

The Times reached out to Combs' representatives, but did not hear back.

A representative from the Federal Bureau of Prisons said they "do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individuals, including quarters assignment, release plans, or whether a particular individual is the subject of allegations, investigations, or sanctions."

Legal troubles hit a high note last year for Combs when he was involved in a lengthy and public trial involving allegations of sexual assault and other violence. His former girlfriend Casandra "Cassie" Ventura and producer Rodney "Lil Rod" Jones lodged civil complaints against the music tycoon.

In July 2025, Combs was found guilty on two counts of a prostitution-related charge, but not guilty of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking, which carried heavier penalties, including a maximum sentence of life in prison.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Nana regaled city’s drama patrons too
articles.summary: Nana Patekar, who died Thursday, is remembered in Lucknow for theatre roles like ‘Purush’, which ran 16 years and revived audience interest.
articles.body: Lucknow: Long before Nana Patekar became known for his powerful dialogues — from “Yeh Musalman ka khoon, yeh Hindu ka khoon…” in Krantiveer in the 1990s to “Control Uday, control” in Welcome — he was a theatre actor.And Lucknow was among the cities that got to experience the actor up close. Nana, who died on Thursday, had a career, of which theatre was an important thread.For Lucknow’s theatre lovers, his legacy is also tied to the stage of Ravindralaya, where the city watched him perform ‘Purush’, the powerful Hindi play in which he played a corrupt politician and sexual predator.Talking to TOI, Lucknow-born theatre director and designer Salim Arif recalled his association with Nana and said his performance in ‘Purush’, which was staged in the city, revealed the extraordinary intensity of an actor who remained “simple and transparent” offstage. The play ran for more than 16 years and clocked around 1,860 shows, bringing together Patekar and actress Ayesha Jhulka. It was directed by celebrated theatre personality Vijaya Mehta.“The production was among the major plays by nationally known actors that came to the city and helped create a renewed appetite for theatre among Lucknow audiences,” said Arif, who worked with Patekar on Gulzar’s ‘Hu Tu Tu’, and said the actor brought value to every role he played.“Just like Rajkumar, Nana too had a distinct style,” he recalled. Patekar, he said, was far removed from the trappings of stardom and would often say that he needed only “200 bucks” to survive and was known for his generosity, even donating a substantial part of his fee to charity. On the sets of ‘Hu Tu Tu’, he would cook prawns and fish and feed the entire unit, Arif recalled. The actor’s simplicity extended to his personal life too, with Arif remembering how Patekar would stay in a modest one-room house during Ganpati celebrations, while his mother would insist that visitors eat before leaving.Veteran Lucknow actor Anil Rastogi, meanwhile, recalled watching Patekar perform on stage in two different productions in Lucknow. “He came to Lucknow twice for the love of theatre. One of his plays was ‘Ek Kunwara Shadi Shuda’, in which he played a servant. Interestingly, he also played a female character. articles.title: Demi Moore almost lost role in “St. Elmo’s Fire” to Madonna after showing up ‘drunk and high’ to fitting
articles.summary: The “Substance” actress previously opened up about having a 24/7 sober companion on the film.
articles.body:
Demi Moore was nearly replaced by Madonna in St. Elmo's Fire.

Director Joel Schumacher allegedly gave Moore an ultimatum: Get sober or get fired.

Moore chose to enter recovery and had a 24/7 sober companion on set.

Demi Moore had to shape up in order to keep her role in St. Elmo's Fire .

Otherwise, director Joel Schumacher would replace her. Troubles on set had begun a couple of weeks before shooting, as costume designer Susan Becker had alerted him to the fact that Moore showed up to a fitting "drunk and high."

"Joel and [producer] Lauren Shuler [Donner] met with Demi and what Joel told me, he told her is, 'Go kill yourself on someone else's movie,'" Carl Kurlander, the film's co-writer, said on the Thursday episode of Reality Life with Kate Casey , noting that Schumacher had his own experiences with addiction. "And Lauren Shuler Donner, God bless her, worked out a plan with Joel, saying, 'Look, if you can clean yourself up in 10 days you can be in this movie.'"

Entertainment Weekly reached out to representatives for Moore for comment.

In the meantime, the production needed to be ready with a backup plan. While he considered several candidates to play Jules, including some existing cast members like Jenny Wright, Schumacher apparently had his eyes set on Madonna.

"Joel had met Madonna. And he came back and he said, 'This girl is going to be the biggest star in the world. I could just feel it,'" Kurlander said. "And Joel was all ready to offer the part to Madonna."

But Moore was not going to give up her chance to be in the 1985 film. She got a sober companion and began attending AA meetings, proving to Schumacher that she was serious about her recovery.

"She clearly had more than just cleaned up," Kurlander said.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Moore has been open about her struggles with substance abuse in the past. In her 2019 memoir Inside Out , she wrote that by the mid '80s, "my appetite for cocaine had escalated into a dependency."

And in the Brats documentary in 2024, which documented the rise of the Brat Pack in the 1980s, Moore shared her perspective on having a sober companion during St. Elmo's Fire. She said that director Schumacher had "stuck his neck out for me" by allowing her to get better and stay in the movie.

"We were all just beginning," she said of herself and her costars. "I didn't have anything to really warrant him sticking by me. They paid to have a sober companion with me 24/7 during the whole shooting."

She was aware that Schumacher could recast her, so the 63-year-old was grateful to have a second chance. Moore would maintain her sobriety for over two decades before relapsing in 2012. After re-entering treatment, she has been sober ever since.

"They could have easily just found someone else," Moore said. "Going to treatment, they were like, 'We want you to check in.' I'm like, 'No, no, I'm starting a movie.' And they said, 'Yes, but what's more important to you: the movie or your life?' And I said, 'The movie! C'mon, what are you talking about?' For me, I didn't have any value for myself. I think I was so fearful of failing."

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s death case: Goa Police registers 'unnatural death' case; to record statements of family and conduct post-mortem to establish cause of death
articles.summary: The Goa Police have registered a medico-legal 'Unnatural Death' (UD) case in connection with the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar.
articles.body: The Goa Police have registered a medico-legal 'Unnatural Death' (UD) case in connection with the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar. As per the latest update on IANS, an inquiry is underway to establish the circumstances and exact cause of the actor's death.As per a post on the IANS official handle, a case has been registered under Section 194 of the BNSS, with PSI Nitin Naik conducting the inquiry. An entry in the case registered at Panjim, stated that the actor was “brought dead to the casualty from Ocean Park, Dona Paula. Accordingly visited the spot at Manipal Hospital Bambolim at concern ward and matter was discussed with Medical Officer.”As part of the investigation, police will conduct an inquest, arrange a post-mortem examination at Goa Medical College (GMC) and record statements from family members and other relevant persons to determine the cause of death.Police are currently examining the circumstances surrounding the actor’s death. If the investigation establishes that the death was due to natural causes, the case may be closed accordingly. However, if any evidence of foul play or other suspicious circumstances emerges, further legal action may follow.This update comes after Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, told the media early Thursday morning, "We tried here to our maximum, but he was brought dead and then we had to make a police case. The body has now been taken to the morgue in Goa Medical College for postmortem. It was a cardiac arrest, but we do not know the cause."The doctor also mentioned, "He was a known cardiac patient and was on medication, as far as we have been told."Patekar, died early Thursday morning after suffering a reported cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. Doctors at Manipal Hospital reportedly administered CPR for around 45 minutes in an attempt to revive him, however, he was declared dead at 5.20 am.The post-mortem examination was reportedly conducted on Thursday morning, after which the actor's mortal remains were released for his last rites. articles.title: 'Nana Patekar's final film 'Shakti Shalini' will be a tribute to the actor': Director Aditya Sarpotdar
articles.summary: Filmmaker Aditya Sarpotdar says he never imagined his upcoming horror-comedy 'Shakti Shalini' would be Nana Patekar's last film and will now ensure it
articles.body: Filmmaker Aditya Sarpotdar says he never imagined his upcoming horror-comedy 'Shakti Shalini' would be Nana Patekar's last film and will now ensure it serves as a fitting "tribute" to one of Indian cinema's finest actors."Shakti Shalini", the next title of Maddock Films' popular horror comedy universe, will posthumously feature Patekar alongside Aneet Padda of 'Saiyaara' fame.'Shakti Shalini' to be a tribute to Nana PatekarAccording to Sarpotdar, the actor, who passed away in the early hours of Thursday after suffering a heart attack in Goa, had completed shooting for the movie in May.He revealed that Patekar had spoken to him about 10 days ago, seeking an update on the film's post-production, and was looking forward to watching the movie."I never expected that 'Shakti Shalini' will be his last film. I'm deeply saddened that this will be his last work. I never thought that he would suddenly step away in this way. I'm unable to process what has actually happened. It (film) is going to be a tribute to one of the best actors of our cinema," Sarpotdar told PTI on phone from Berlin.Aditya Sarpotdar on narrating 'Shakti Shalini' script to Nana PatekarThe director, who is also a family friend of the celebrated actor, shared that he had approached Patekar twice for two of his earlier Marathi films, but things did not materialise."For him the script was the most important thing. If he liked the script, he would do the film; if not, then he wouldn't. I had written those two films keeping him in mind, and there's no replacement for him in Marathi cinema. He wasn't excited about it (film) and hence it didn't happen."The director recalled narrating the script of "Shakti Shalini" to Patekar at his farmhouse in Pune, after which the actor immediately agreed to join the project."He liked the story, his role, Aneet's role and the world that we were creating as well as the things we are talking about in the film. He was excited about 'Shakti Shalini'. We rather stayed for a few days at his farmhouse and had discussions and jammed over the script. He liked having a collaborative process," he said, without divulging details about Patekar's role in the movie."He wouldn't watch every film but he was aware about the horror-comedy universe, he had liked what we had made ('Stree', 'Munjya'). He only had good things to talk about it," the director added.Aditya Sarpotdar on working with Nana PatekarWorking with the 75-year-old actor turned out to be an enriching experience for Sarpotdar, who described Patekar as a "power house of a talent" and "childlike" person."He was always excited and inquisitive to know newer things, like he was interested to know about VFX, the thought process of the young actors and technicians, their working style, etc," he said.Aditya Sarpotdar admits Nana Patekar yelled at himSpeaking about Patekar's well-known outspoken nature and temper on the sets, Sarpotdar said he was occasionally reprimanded by the actor but never took it to heart."Yes, of course, he yelled at me. He would yell 'haq se'. He wanted everyone to put their best foot forward. He was a senior and experienced actor, and he had a point of view. He would want to express that, talk, discuss things, which he believed was good for the film and the filmmaker," he said.According to the filmmaker, Patekar's anger never lasted long."...Within five minutes he would come back, either pat me on the back, feed me something or hug me. That was the most endearing thing about him. You would automatically forget that he had yelled at you," he said.Nana Patekar's final films before death'Shakti Shalini', produced by Dinesh Vijan via his banner Maddock Films, is reportedly expected to arrive in theatres in March 2027.In addition to this film, Patekar will also be seen in the Shraddha Kapoor-starrer "Eetha", slated for release in December 2026, and director Anant Mahadevan's "The Confession of Mary".Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce branded ‘absentee’ owners over $5.35 million Ohio mansion; neighbours raise sewage, wildlife and security fears while couple’s team defends scaled-back fence and preserved access
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over plans to increase privacy and security at their $5.35 million mansion in
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are facing objections from neighbours over plans to increase privacy and security at their $5.35 million mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio. The couple's proposed six-foot fence and extensive landscaping have sparked a dispute with longtime residents, who have raised concerns ranging from potential damage to a shared sewer line to wildlife safety and privacy.According to the Daily Mail, the disagreement has continued through local planning and architectural review meetings, with officials approving parts of the couple's proposals while asking them to revise other plans.Neighbour calls the new owner an 'absentee owner'Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door to the property for 35 years, reportedly described the arrival of the new owner as a major disruption to the peace and quiet of the Lake Erie village.At a meeting of Bratenahl's Architectural Review Board last month, Bolton criticised the prospect of an owner who would not be present at the property regularly.“There's a new owner, who is an absentee owner, who is not going to be here,” she said, according to the hearing transcript cited by the Daily Mail.The report said the couple's names were not mentioned during the 72-page transcript of that meeting. However, at a subsequent hearing on Tuesday, Bolton explicitly identified the property as having been purchased by Kelce.The mansion reportedly spans 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and a two-bedroom guest cottage. Built in 1895, the estate also features a ballroom that has been converted into a game room and home theatre.Shared sewer line becomes a major point of contentionOne of Bolton's principal concerns involves a century-old clay sewer pipe shared by her home and the mansion.She told the board that she had received an estimate of $75,000 to line the pipe to protect it against tree-root intrusion. Her concerns intensified after learning about the couple's proposed landscaping, which reportedly included planting around 50 evergreen trees near the sewer line.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure and catastrophic sewage backups,” Bolton told the meeting, citing research she said she had conducted using artificial intelligence.She also questioned whether the new owners would remain in the area long enough to deal with any problems that might arise.The couple's project representatives disputed the criticism. Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction told the board that Bolton had planted arborvitae trees directly over the sewer line, closer to it than the trees proposed by the new owners.Property manager Patrick Hyland also said the owners had spent $7,500 of their own money to replace a damaged section of the shared sewer line and had arranged for the entire line to be cleaned.According to the Daily Mail, the couple's team also said it had added gates to preserve Bolton's access to the sewer.Residents question fence design and security plansChuck Bauernschmidt, who has lived two doors away for 39 years, raised concerns about the removal of vegetation from the property. He presented photographs to the board and criticised what he described as the extensive clearing of shrubs and trees.“It's now ridiculous,” he said, according to the hearing transcript. “All the trees are gone.”Bauernschmidt also questioned the proposed fence's spear-topped design, warning that deer could become caught on its points. Village official Mary Ranney reportedly acknowledged that such incidents occur occasionally.Bolton's husband, Bill, a former president of the Bratenahl village council, raised further concerns about whether the fence would provide meaningful protection against paparazzi. He argued that a fence measuring five or six feet would not necessarily deter someone determined to look into the property.He also pointed to potential security threats from drones and Lake Erie, questioning how the owners might respond to unauthorised aerial surveillance.Board approves some plans but asks for revisionsThe couple's representatives reportedly said they had initially considered an eight-foot fence extending approximately 1,190 feet around the lakefront estate. Following discussions, the proposal was scaled back to a six-foot fence, which was unanimously approved at the earlier meeting despite objections from neighbours.The approved fence will replace an existing five-foot structure, sit two feet farther inside the property boundary and stop short of Lake Erie.At Tuesday's hearing, the board approved the proposed landscaping at the front of the estate, subject to conditions ensuring the trees on the southern side have sufficient room to mature.However, it declined to approve a proposed line of saplings along the shoreline, citing concerns about their eventual height. The couple's team must return with a revised landscaping plan.Photographs cited by the Daily Mail reportedly show landscaping work already underway, with sections of turf removed and bare ground visible. A “no trespassing” sign has also been placed at the entrance.Couple's team says it has tried to accommodate neighboursDespite the objections, representatives for Swift and Kelce told the board they had made several changes in an effort to maintain good relations with nearby residents.Kutz said the fence had been moved farther inside the property's boundary and that the plan to extend it to the water had been dropped. The team also said it had paid to cut back trees on the Boltons' and Stephensons' properties and had installed an additional gate after Bauernschmidt complained that he felt closed off.The property manager reportedly said neighbours would continue to be allowed to cross the back gardens with permission.Kutz also presented photographs to challenge claims that the estate's grounds had been stripped of healthy vegetation, arguing that the property had previously been heavily overgrown and poorly maintained.Not all residents opposed the changes. Victoria Broer, who chaired Bratenahl's planning commission for nearly 20 years, reportedly welcomed the decision to keep the fence away from the shoreline.“I do appreciate that the fence is not going all the way to the lake, because that would be in my view,” she said.Property records cited by the Daily Mail indicate that the mansion was purchased in March by a limited liability company linked to Kelce. The company had been incorporated in Ohio on February 26 and was used to acquire the property a week later.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Olivia Colman on viral Wicker memes: 'This has never happened to me before'
articles.summary: Steamy jokes have flooded social media ahead of the release of the actress's latest film.
articles.body:
It has already been described as 2026's weirdest rom-com .

And new film Wicker has sparked a deluge of viral memes and steamy jokes that have flooded social media ahead of its release.

Speaking to the BBC at its London Film Festival premiere, lead star Olivia Colman said she never expected such a big reaction.

"No, literally this has never happened for anything I've done before," she said.

"But you put Alexander Skarsgård in an interesting outfit, and everyone is looking."

The film tells the tale of a lonely, ostracised fisherwoman (Colman) living in a medieval village.

Tired of constantly being mocked for being single, she hires a basketmaker to mould her a new partner made entirely out of wicker.

Enter Skarsgård - but not as you've ever seen him before.

As the "wicker husband", he emerges as a strapping, dashing life-size piece of furniture.

And he proves to be a devoted partner, and passionate lover, sparking jealousy among the other village women.

The film has an A-list cast, with other stars including Peter Dinklage as the basket weaver, Elizabeth Debicki as the tailor's wife, and Richard E Grant as the village doctor.

Since the release of the trailer, there's been a huge buzz online around the film - from BookTok and FilmTok fans swooning over Skarsgård’s character, to questions being asked over splinter risks during the film's erotic scenes.

Swedish giant Ikea even got involved, posting photos of its rattan furniture on Instagram in a nod to the film, with the caption “husband material”.

When asked why she thinks people are so fascinated and so thirsty for the wicker husband, Colman answered: "We all love a little bit of escapism. That's what film is beautiful for.

"And it's magical, and a bit of fantasy, and people love that, especially currently. What's not to love about a little bit of escapism and fantasy?"

She also said it was the film's originality that drew her to it.

"You get a lot of scripts through the post, and you feel like you've seen a bit before. And this, I really hadn't seen this before, so I was excited," she said.

Like Colman, Debicki agrees that Skarsgård is the main reason the film has lit up the internet.

"I think it was a lot to do with Alex in a wicker man costume, really," she told the BBC. "I think that's something that apparently everybody would like to see."

But Skarsgård himself gives all the credit to the designers of the outfit. "All I had to do was get stuck into it," he says.

He also said the sex scenes were "super fun" to shoot.

"We wanted those moments when the bed crashes and breaks, and the way they comment on that in the scene is quite comedic," he said.

"But [the characters] also have tender moments and sexy moments, it was great."

The film is based on the short story The Wicker Husband by Ursula Wills-Jones.

After its premiere at Sundance film festival earlier this year, The Guardian awarded it two stars, praising the "eye-catching premise" but cautioning that there was "too much wood but not enough fire".

But The Hollywood Reporter was more positive, calling it "a warming, sometimes poignant pleasure".

Away from the social media buzz, the film's stars say it also taps into deeper themes, from gender roles to breaking societal rules.

"It's very funny and strange and wonderful, but I find it very moving. And it's a good one to discover beyond the Ikea memes," said Debicki.

"It touches on a lot of stuff. Hierarchy, social structure," said Skarsgård. "But it's done with such a light touch."

"It's about love, and it is funny, but it's also a romance, and it very gently laughs at the sort of traditions we have in marriage and community," said Colman.

"I think it's something that you will come out and discuss a lot."

Wicker is released in UK cinemas on October 30.

articles.summary: Aaron Sorkin's "The Social Reckoning" faced blistering critiques from both conservatives and liberals and sits at 59% on Rotten Tomatoes.
articles.body: "The Social Reckoning," the follow-up to the 2010 hit "The Social Network," is facing blistering critiques from both sides of the political spectrum alongside lukewarm reviews from critics, with some reviewers sharply criticizing the film's political messaging and its handling of Facebook's role in American politics. "The Social Network" focused on the creation of Facebook and the legal battle over its ownership, earning three Oscars, including for screenwriter Aaron Sorkin, and a 96% positive rating on review-aggregation website Rotten Tomatoes. It's more political follow-up, "The Social Reckoning," written and directed by Sorkin, has received a more mixed response, with a 61% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes as of Thursday evening. DAVID MARCUS: WOKE 1.0 IS WHY ENTERTAINERS NEEDED OUR SECRET CONSERVATIVE CLUB Earlier this year, a trailer debuted showing Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg (played by Jeremy Strong) being questioned by a character played by comedian Bill Burr. In the scene, Zuckerberg defends online free speech and argues that users are responsible for their own behavior. Burr’s character vigorously challenges him. Sorkin published an open letter in 2019 criticizing Zuckerberg’s management of the platform. OutKick writer Ian Miller was one of several conservative critics who mocked the trailer as tone-deaf, replying, "It is the most Hollywood thing ever to desperately try and convince everyone that the guy making complete sense is the bad guy and the one demanding authoritarian ideological enforcement is the good guy." Film critics were also sharply critical. The Globe and Mail film critic Barry Hertz tweeted that the film was "one of the most insipid, ugly, flat films of the year — an insufferably sanctimonious fantasia of blue-state Boomers." In his actual review, he argued that the movie is counterproductive in that it "will turn even the most hardcore Facebook hater into a true-blue Facebook believer — the film is just that magnificently, unbelievably, despicably bad." Variety said it badly missed the original's director David Fincher and "already feels behind the curve," while Wired magazine’s review described the new film as one that "already feels irrelevant." Wired noted that the movie opens with the DUI arrest of a woman who directs racist, right-wing insults at police officers and is arrested for threatening to kill one of them. When the video goes viral, a Facebook whistleblower recognizes the woman as a former liberal acquaintance from her Pilates class. The film's climax, as noted by Wired, is the Jan. 6, 2021, capitol riot, "the horrors of which are blamed in part on Facebook’s failure to either get a handle on election fraud conspiracy theories or remove Donald Trump’s account as he stoked such inflammatory falsehoods." "Now, halfway into Trump’s second term, is it all that much of a revelation that he and his movement are emboldened by the complicity of tech oligarchs, who openly backed him in 2024?" the outlet asked. CHRIS MURPHY CALLS FOR 'REGULATING THE INTERNET' SO PEOPLE WON'T FALL FOR A 'DEMAGOGUE LIKE DONALD TRUMP' Journalist and film critic Stephen Silver described the movie as "an old-man-yells-at-cloud treatment of Facebook." Silver wrote that Sorkin essentially argues Facebook was not censorious enough in the 2010s and that the government should now step in by reforming Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, a federal law that generally shields online platforms from liability for content posted by users. "No, I don’t buy that Facebook is primarily responsible for American political extremism, or for January 6," Silver wrote, arguing that individuals remain responsible for their own actions online. SFGate's Lindsey Bahr wrote that while certain political aspects hit the mark, the movie falls far short of its predecessor: "It is unfortunate for ‘The Social Reckoning’ that ‘The Social Network’ exists." IndieWire was even harsher, panning its script and performances. The BBC's reviewer gave it two out of five stars, calling it unlikely to influence anyone, while The Guardian in a mixed review dismissed it as a "film which doesn’t reckon with the future we’re living in." Even some reviews rated as positive on Rotten Tomatoes were tepid in their assessments. A review from The Seattle Times said it moved "snappily" but was still a "pale imitation" of "The Social Network." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Media Research Center President David Bozell commented on the film's political messaging to Fox News Digital. "It says everything you need to know about Aaron Sorkin and the Hollywood elite that they would make a movie suggesting Big Tech’s real failure was not censoring conservatives enough," Bozell said. "The Media Research Center spent years exposing how Facebook suppressed conservative voices, and we were right to do it," he continued. "Mark Zuckerberg eventually acknowledged Meta’s past censorship abuses and took meaningful steps to move the company back toward a more open platform. Meta is far from perfect, but Zuckerberg deserves some credit for redirecting it away from the censorship monster it had become. "Hollywood seems determined to fight yesterday’s battle even as Zuckerberg has moved on from it," Bozell added. "Americans have had enough of government-imposed censorship, ideological gatekeeping and Big Tech deciding which political views they are allowed to hear." articles.title: Malhar Patekar on father Nana Patekar's legacy: 'His achievements have made him immortal' - WATCH
articles.summary: Veteran actor Nana Patekar's son Malhar Patekar said his father's work has made him immortal and that his vision, particularly his social initiatives
articles.body: Veteran actor Nana Patekar's son Malhar Patekar said his father's work has made him immortal and that his vision, particularly his social initiatives through the Naam Foundation, would be carried forward even after his demise.Speaking to reporters about his father's legacy, Malhar Patekar said, "A person like Nana Saheb never truly leaves us; his achievements have made him immortal. Secondly, he always believed that everyone should come together and follow a righteous path on a global scale. Thirdly, regarding the future-carrying forward the vision Nana Saheb left behind is how we will shape the life ahead."Elaborating on his father's vision and the work of the organisation, Malhar said, "Through our organisation, work was already underway in the water sector, and large-scale initiatives in education and health had begun in Kashmir as well. Thirdly, he assigned specific responsibilities to everyone before he left."Regarding the Marathwada work, he said, "I spoke to the Chief Minister just a short while ago, and he noted that the work being done through the Naam Foundation is proceeding under the guidance of our CEO, Ganesh Thorat. The Chief Minister acknowledged that we have collaborated in the past, but he emphasised that Nana Saheb had intended to push even harder this time around. So, the Chief Minister stated that we must ensure that what he had envisioned actually comes to pass."On the decision to conduct the last rites late Thursday night, Malhar said, "We proceeded (with the last rites today) because the tragedy occurred early this morning, so a significant amount of time had already passed. That is why we decided to go ahead with it today."Nana Patekar died after suffering a severe cardiac arrest. He was taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for around 45 minutes. Dr Shekhar Salkar, Chief of the Oncology Department at Manipal Hospital, confirmed the news to ANI. articles.body:
Giuliano Eriston em fotos superpostas na capa do álbum ao vivo em que o cantor rebobina as músicas do recente álbum autoral 'Politonia' — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Cinco anos após ter sido o campeão da edição de 2021 do programa The Voice Brasil (TV Globo), em temporada na qual interpretou canções alheias como “Luz do sol” (Caetano Veloso, 1982) e “A rota do indivíduo” (Djavan, 1991), o cantor, compositor e violonista Giuliano Eriston tenta se consolidar como intérprete de repertório autoral.

Entre o EP “Giuliano Eriston interpreta Sérgio Sampaio” (2024), o artista lançou dois álbuns autorais, “Universo em si” (2022) e “Politonia” (2026).

É o repertório deste segundo álbum autoral – lançado em 28 de abril com músicas que refletem os sentimentos decorrentes da migração do cantor cearense para a cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) – que Eriston rebobina no álbum “Politonia – Voz & violão – Ao vivo”.

Nos aplicativos de áudio e nos canais oficiais de vídeo do artista desde ontem, sexta-feira, 8 de outubro, o álbum “Politonia – Voz & violão – Ao vivo” rebobina as nove músicas do álbum “Politonia” – “Lucidez”, “Gosto do gesto”, “Festa do infinito”, “Corpo de candiá”, “Borogodó”, “Não pro sim”, “Vem me relembrar”, “Teia” e “Waiting” – em registros captados ao vivo em pocket show feito por Eriston nos Estúdios Mega, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), para plateia formada por cerca de 70 convidados.

A gravação ao vivo foi feita com produção musical de Pedro Baby e do próprio Giuliano Eriston. Pedro Baby e Sérgio Almeida assinam a mixagem e a masterização.

articles.title: Hope - O primeiro impacto: Hoyeon defende filme mais caro da Coreia | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Quantos diretores no mundo conseguiriam fazer um filme tão louco?', diz Hoyeon, em entrevista ao g1. Ficção científica de Na Hong-jin exibida em Cannes custou US$ 46 milhões.
articles.summary: Em entrevista ao g1, Hoyeon comenta os bastidores de Hope - O primeiro impacto, ficção científica de Na Hong-jin que custou US$ 46 milhões.
articles.body:
Filme mais caro da história da Coreia do Sul, "Hope - O primeiro impacto" divide opiniões de público e de críticos desde sua exibição na competição pela Palma de Ouro do Festival de Cannes, em maio.

Uma das maiores estrelas do elenco, Hoyeon tem orgulho da divisão gerada pela ficção científica, que custou estimados US$ 46 milhões e estreou nesta quinta-feira (8) nos cinemas brasileiros.

"Mesmo com um orçamento considerado enorme para a Coreia, e todas as pressões práticas da realidade, ter um diretor que se mantém fiel à sua visão é precioso demais. Por isso, ver o público se dividir entre quem ama e odeia é a coisa mais natural do mundo. Quebrar expectativas é fascinante", diz a atriz de 32 anos em entrevista ao g1 .

"Sendo sincera, quantos diretores no mundo conseguiriam fazer um filme tão louco — no bom sentido — como este? Acho que poucos."

Em "Hope", a modelo interpreta uma policial em perseguição atrás de uma criatura misteriosa, que tem deixado um rastro de destruição e morte em um pequeno vilarejo de pescadores.

Em seu primeiro trabalho mais relevante desde que se tornou a grande revelação da primeira temporada do fenômeno mundial "Round 6", Hoyeon reverencia Na Hong-jin, que assina a direção e o roteiro do filme. Ela não é a única.

O último filme do cineasta de 52 anos, "O lamento" (2016), é considerado por muitos um dos melhores terrores do século — e tem até hoje uma aprovação de 99% dos críticos do site agregador Rotten Tomatoes.

"O que me fez achar o diretor Na um gênio foi algo que li em uma crítica: 'O lamento' pega uma história simples e a desenvolve de forma complexa. 'Hope' pega uma história complexa e a desenvolve de forma simples", afirma a atriz.

"Quem assistiu a 'O lamento' e esperava o próximo filme dele jamais imaginaria uma comédia. Achei essa escolha genial. O filme desafia as expectativas da plateia o tempo todo: quando você acha que vai acontecer tal coisa, ele vai para outro lado e joga piadas. Isso foi totalmente intencional."

Hoyeon em cena de 'Round 6' — Foto: Divulgação

Leia abaixo a entrevista na íntegra, editada para clareza (com tradução de Julie Kim):

Hoyeon - Bem. Hoje é meu dia de folga. Estive trabalhando, filmando uma série, e tem sido muito bom. Hoje é um dia relaxante, com exceção desta entrevista. Acho que vou comer um kimchi-jjigae depois daqui.

g1 - Parece uma boa ideia. Kimchi-jjigae é ótimo e aqui está bem na hora da janta. Parabéns pelo filme. Demora bastante tempo até a sua primeira cena neste filme, mas ela é muito marcante. O quanto você conversou com o diretor Na sobre o que aconteceu com a sua personagem até aquele momento?

Hoyeon - Assim como o Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) e o Sung-ki (Zo In-sung), depois da transmissão no rádio, pela própria personalidade extrema da Sung-ae, ela pegou todas as armas que estavam no depósito da delegacia e saiu com tudo.

Ela realmente juntou todas as armas que pôde, levou com ela e já estava andando por aí para ajudar as pessoas do vilarejo. Foi sobre isso que conversei com o diretor.

Se você reparar bem, a caracterização dos machucados da Sung-ae mostra que ela já vinha rolando no chão e passando por perrengues. Para mostrar isso, entendi e atuei pensando que não era como se ela estivesse encarando aquela situação pela primeira vez — embora, para o público, seja a primeira vez que a veem.

g1 - O cinema coreano das últimas décadas ficou muito conhecido por lidar com temas sociais e luta de classes. Este filme é mais voltado para a ação e lida com essa criatura que, durante a primeira metade, a gente nem consegue ver direito. O que faz deste filme uma história universal? Ter que enfrentar uma ameaça desconhecida torna a história universal?

Hoyeon - Filmes como "Parasita" (2019) ou o novo do diretor Lee Chang-dong, "Amor possível", tratam de classes de um jeito bem coreano, mas acho que também dá para dizer que são histórias universais.

No caso de "Hope", pegamos uma história muito universal e fizemos um filme de ação comercial, de entretenimento. Mas acho que todas as histórias, quando olhamos de perto, parecem casos muito individuais, só que no fim das contas a história daquela pessoa não é tão diferente da minha, nem da de alguém que vive em outro país.

Os seres humanos, por mais diferentes que pareçam — será que o modo de vida deles é tão diferente assim? Fico sempre pensando nisso.

Hoyeon e Hwang Jung-min em cena de 'Hope: O primeiro impacto' — Foto: Divulgação

g1 - O que faz do diretor Na um cineasta tão único?

Hoyeon - A forma como ele enxerga o mundo é muito especial. Conversando com o diretor, penso muito: "Nossa, dá para olhar por esse ângulo também". Ele pensa na situação e nas consequências que ela vai trazer, mas também capta a intenção das pessoas com muita precisão.

Ele percebe as coisas rápido demais: a intenção de alguém, a situação em si e o resultado daquilo. Aprendi muito durante as filmagens. O olhar dele sobre o mundo é muito rápido e, às vezes, me pego pensando: "Ele repara até nesse tipo de detalhe, até nessa intenção?". Coisas que uma pessoa comum nem pensaria.

É justamente por enxergar tudo dessa maneira que ele consegue escrever roteiros assim e ter uma imaginação tão única.

g1 - Este é um filme muito ambicioso. A primeira hora é uma sequência de ação tão maluca e tão boa que escrevi que é a melhor primeira hora do ano todo no cinema, com folga. Mas ele também dividiu opiniões. Vocês já esperavam reações tão intensas, desde o Festival de Cannes até na Coreia? Há muito o que processar, já que o filme tem partes muito diferentes entre si.

Hoyeon - Desde a fase do roteiro até ver o resultado final, achei um filme absurdamente engraçado, o melhor entretenimento possível. Adorei todo o humor.

Ao ler o roteiro, o que me fez achar o diretor um gênio foi algo que li em uma crítica:

"O lamento" pega uma história simples e a desenvolve de forma complexa; "Hope" pega uma história complexa e a desenvolve de forma simples. Concordei muito com isso.

Kunimura Jun em cena de 'O lamento' — Foto: Divulgação

Se ele tentasse repetir a fórmula de "O lamento", será que sairia algo superior? Acho difícil, nunca saberemos. Mas, mantendo a identidade dele, ele transformou isso em algo cômico.

Quem assistiu a "O lamento" e esperava o próximo filme dele jamais imaginaria uma comédia. Achei essa escolha genial. O filme desafia as expectativas da plateia o tempo todo: quando você acha que vai acontecer tal coisa, ele vai para outro lado e joga piadas. Isso foi totalmente intencional.

E, sendo sincera, quantos diretores no mundo conseguiriam fazer um filme tão louco — no bom sentido — como este? Acho que poucos. Ter uma identidade própria, bancar suas ambições e, mesmo com um orçamento considerado enorme para a Coreia e todas as pressões práticas da realidade, ter um diretor que se mantém fiel à sua visão é precioso demais.

Por isso, ver o público se dividir entre quem ama e odeia é a coisa mais natural do mundo. Quebrar expectativas é fascinante. Diretores como ele precisam continuar existindo e fazendo os filmes que querem, do jeito deles, seja qual for o gênero. Trabalhar com ele e vivenciar "Hope" foi uma experiência empolgante e eletrizante para mim como cinéfila, não importa o que digam.

articles.title: Rochelle Jordan fala sobre Beyoncé, Liniker e estreia no Brasil: 'Vou dar o meu melhor para as garotas' | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora canadense, que mistura R&B com drum and bass e house, se apresenta no Zig Festival neste sábado (11). Leia entrevista dela ao g1.
articles.summary: Cantora canadense, que mistura R&B com drum and bass e house, se apresenta no Zig Festival neste sábado (11). Leia entrevista dela ao g1.
articles.body:
Rochelle Jordan vem ao Brasil para o Zig Festival — Foto: Divulgação

Quem nunca ouviu "Through the Wall", álbum de Rochelle Jordan, está perdendo música dançante de altíssima qualidade. A artista canadense vem ao Brasil pela primeira vez neste sábado (10), para o Zig Festival, que conta com a americana Slayyyter e a dupla Haute & Freddy entre as atrações.

Rochelle traz uma música de pista que dá para chamar de "chique". Há anos, a artista mescla vocais e elementos de R&B com batidas de drum and bass, house e UK garage para criar seu repertório.

Em resenhas internacionais, seu trabalho costuma aparecer junto de expressões como "à frente do seu tempo".

"Sempre estou ouvindo o que já foi para poder criar o que será. É assim que vejo as coisas", disse a canadense ao g1 .

Rochelle começou a compor ainda adolescente e lançou várias mixtapes nos anos 2010. O primeiro disco dela, "1021", veio em 2014. Na época, ela não se deu bem com o contrato de gravadora, passou por problemas de saúde e ficou fora por um tempo.

Sete anos depois, a artista voltou pra valer com o disco "Play With The Changes" (2021), que já explorava vertentes da dance music.

Rochelle explica que se espelha em artistas "diferentes e vanguardistas", como a dupla Neptunes e as cantoras Kelis e Aaliyah. "No início, eu dizia [ao produtor KLSH]: 'Me dê a sua batida mais estranha', e conseguia escrever em cima disso".

"Acho que essa fundação central de tentarmos coisas novas e sermos destemidos é o que nos trouxe até aqui. (...) Nós seguimos os passos de pensar: o que podemos fazer que seja fora da caixa, mas ainda assim acessível? Como isso soa para nós?".

Cantora canadense Rochelle Jordan vem ao Brasil para o Zig Festival — Foto: Divulgação

"Depois de cada álbum que fazemos, eu fico pensando: 'Acho que nunca mais vou escrever uma música, esse foi o meu melhor trabalho, isso nunca mais vai acontecer'. Eu passo por esse estágio estranho de me sentir assim, mas sabe de uma coisa? Fica melhor a cada vez".

A julgar pela recepção, de fato tem ficado cada vez melhor. "Play With The Changes" apareceu em várias listas de "melhores do ano". Seu sucessor, "Through the Wall" (2025), foi ainda mais elogiado.

Tudo isso tem rendido: neste ano, Rochelle foi convidada para fazer um remix de Mariah Carey em uma edição colaborativa do disco "Glitter". Circula por aí que ela esteve entre as inspirações de Madonna na criação do álbum "Confessions II".

Rochelle não sabe dizer se isso procede, mas acredita, sim, que seu trabalho tenha influência no pop — inclusive no "Renaissance", de Beyoncé, que ela define como "álbum absolutamente incrível da diva de uma geração".

"Sinto que, na minha mente, o 'Play with the Changes' tocou muitas pessoas em termos de influência. Acho que há muito crédito para aquele álbum porque ele encorajou a mente da diáspora negra a entender que você pode ser um vocalista de R&B e contar uma história em cima de uma batida de drum and bass ou de house. Obviamente, se voltarmos a Cevin Fisher, Robin S, Corona e Crystal Waters, era isso o que eles faziam, mas isso se perdeu por um bom tempo."

"Acredito verdadeiramente que o 'Play with the Changes' focou nisso e acordou grande parte da indústria. Então, quando ouvi o 'Renaissance' depois disso, pensei: 'Será que [o meu álbum] tocou a Beyoncé?' Possivelmente, ou pelo menos motivou a ideia. E não há nada de errado com isso, é lindo, porque é uma retomada desse som, já que as pessoas negras foram as que iniciaram o movimento house e disco. Então, pertence a nós tocá-lo".

Se Rochelle influenciou algo no trabalho de Beyoncé, a diva pop a inspirou de volta. "Fiquei muito motivada ao ouvir a Beyoncé fazer seu grande trabalho na música house com o 'Renaissance' e depois veio o 'Through the Wall'. Mas o 'Through the Wall' também foi feito ouvindo novamente Anita Baker e Aaliyah. Eu sempre crio a partir dessa base. Até mesmo sobre a Beyoncé, penso no álbum 'Dangerously in Love'. Sempre estou ouvindo o que já foi para criar o que será".

'Ápice da animação' para vinda ao Brasil

Para sua estreia no Brasil, Rochelle está para lá de ansiosa. Ao descobrir que o Zig Festival pertence à Zig, principal balada LGBTQ+ de São Paulo, Rochelle ficou ainda mais animada: "Tenho que dar o meu melhor para as garotas!".

Rochelle Jordan no clipe de 'Doing It Too' — Foto: Divulgação

Os planos dela por aqui incluem encontrar Liniker, a quem ela conheceu em um festival na Holanda, há alguns meses. "Ela é uma vocalista maravilhosa, deslumbrante e uma artista excepcional. E está arrasando", diz.

Mais do que isso, Rochelle quer descobrir nossa música ("gostaria de usar o Shazam e criar minha própria playlist", conta) e a nossa comida.

"Me lembra a comida caribenha que cresci comendo: amo as bananas da terra, amo o modo como vocês cozinham o frango, amo os feijões, o arroz, gosto de tudo. Sinto que é um espelho da cultura em que cresci", conta a artista, de família jamaicana.

articles.title: 'Tonight, Tonight', 30 anos depois: clipe tem ligação com Bob Esponja, filme mudo e 'Mundo de Beakman' | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo clássico do Smashing Pumpkins ganhou seis prêmios do VMA da MTV com produção que inspirada no curta 'Viagem à Lua', do diretor francês Georges Méliès.
articles.summary: Vídeo clássico do Smashing Pumpkins ganhou seis prêmios do VMA da MTV com produção que inspirada no curta 'Viagem à Lua', do diretor francês Georges Méliès.
articles.body:
Muita gente ainda se lembra da época em que a MTV exibia o clipe de "Tonight, Tonight", do Smashing Pumpkins. Mas o que nem todo mundo sabe é que este vídeo, que completa 30 anos em 2026, tem ligações diretas com Bob Esponja, "Pequena Miss Sunshine", "Mundo de Beakman" e o primeiro filme de ficção científica do cinema.

A referência mais óbvia é o universo dos filmes mudos. A história é quase um resumo da trama de "Viagem à Lua", curta lançado em 1902 pelo diretor francês Georges Méliès, pioneiro da ficção científica.

A homenagem foi a forma encontrada pela banda para manter a mesma estética da capa de "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness", álbum de onde a música foi retirada.

Capa do álbum 'Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness' e cena do filme 'Viagem à Lua', do francês Georges Méliès — Foto: Reprodução

Toda a parte visual do clipe prendia o espectador desavisado pelos olhos. Os cenários teatrais foram pintados à mão e a produção foi feita quase sem efeitos digitais. Fumaça, marionetes e truques visuais bem antigos dão uma cara única ao clipe.

Quem teve a ideia de seguir esse caminho foi o casal de diretores californianos Jonathan Dayton e Valerie Faris. Dez anos após o lançamento de "Tonight, Tonight", eles dirigiram "Pequena Miss Sunshine", filme que acabou ganhando dois prêmios no Oscar.

Clipe 'Tonight, Tonight', do Smashing Pumpkins, completa 30 anos em 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Jonathan e Valerie trabalharam ao lado do diretor de arte Wayne White. Na mesma época em que gravava com o Smashing Pumpkins, ele era diretor de arte e cenógrafo do "Mundo de Beakman", programa de experiências científicas que marcou a geração que cresceu assistindo aos programas da TV Cultura.

Ainda falta mencionar mais um casal importante para a concepção do clipe: os protagonistas. Tom Kenny e Jill Talley, casados na vida real, trabalhavam no programa de humor "Mr. Show", comandado por Bob Odenkirk (o Saul de "Breaking Bad" e Better Call Saul) e David Cross (o Dr. Tobias de "Arrested Development").

Depois dessa fase, Tom e Jill ficaram mundialmente famosos como as vozes originais dos personagens Bob Esponja e Karen Plâncton.

A mistura de referências fez sucesso imediato e o clipe de "Tonight, Tonight" levou seis prêmios no MTV Video Music Awards de 1996. Hoje, o Smashing Pumpkins segue na ativa sob a liderança do vocalista Billy Corgan.

Tom Kenny e Jill Talley no clipe de 'Tonight, Tonight', do Smashing Pumpkins — Foto: Reprodução

articles.summary: Disco tem edição programada para 30 de outubro e traz 12 músicas do cancioneiro de Mateus Aleluia.

Alan de Deus (à esquerda), Álvaro Lancellotti (de camiseta), Pedro Costa e Michele Leal integram o núcleo central do coletivo Pra Gira Girar — Foto: Felipe Oneill / Divulgação

♬ Um ano após as edições dos singles “Atabaque chora” (2025) e “Deixa a gira girar” (2025), lançados em outubro e novembro do ano passado, respectivamente, o coletivo Pra Gira Girar apresenta em 30 de outubro o primeiro álbum, “Pra gira girar – Uma celebração aos Tincoãs”, pelo selo Amor in Sound.

Com capa que expõe arte de Ilana Paterman Brasil, o álbum reúne 12 músicas extraídas da discografia dos Os Tincoãs, grupo baiano formado em Cachoeira (BA) em 1960 e projetado na década de 1970 com música afro-brasileira de grande carga ancestral e espiritual.

O álbum “Pra gira girar – Uma celebração aos Tincoãs” foi gravado com produção musical orquestrada por Mario Caldato com a colaboração do baixista Alexandre Kassin. O núcleo central do coletivo Pra Gira Girar é composto pelo mentor do grupo, Alvaro Lancellotti (voz), com Alan de Deus (voz), Michele Leal (voz) e Pedro Costa (guitarra).

O repertório do álbum inclui músicas como “A força da Jurema” (Mateus Aleluia, Dadinho e Heraldo Bozas, 1973), “Cordeiro de Nanã” (Mateus Aleulia e Dadinho, 1977), “Lamento às águas” (Mateus Aleluia e Dadinho, 1977), “Na beira do mar” (Mateus Aleluia e Dadinho, 1973), “Oxossi te chama” (Mateus Aleulia e Dadinho, 1975) e “Salmo” (Mateus Aleulia e Dadinho, 1975), entre outras composições da fase áurea dos Tincoãs.

Além do quarteto integrante do núcleo central, o álbum “Pra gira girar – Uma celebração aos Tincoãs” foi gravado com as adesões de Kassin (baixo, além da coprodução), Anna Magalhães (percussão), Diogo Gomes (trompete) e Zé Manoel (piano e voz). O percussionista Zero Awá (1957 – 2025) completa i n memoriam a ficha técnica do disco, editado em LP.

O álbum decorre da boa receptividade do show apresentado pelo coletivo para reverenciar os Tincoãs. “Esse disco é uma consequência do show, nada tínhamos planejado. No entanto, entendemos que essa obra era riquíssima e que pouca gente viu Os Tincoãs em cena. Eles não fizeram tantas aparições como banda e também pertencem a uma geração muito antiga. Houve, então, uma vontade muito genuína de reapresentá-los”, explica Alvaro Lancellotti.
